messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'orbitly-dedicated' node gpu-node-7 reported GPU fan fault + kernel panic. Drain started automatically. Affected tenant: orbitly (VPC, dedicated). Severity: Sev2. Pager: @sanjay. Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/1878001234

sanjay: got the page, on it. starting triage. are there live pods on that node? any model-serving tasks pinned?

leah: copying. i see 3 active pods currently on gpu-node-7 (model-worker-prod x2, batch-infer-queue x1). initiating drain now.

aj: fyi, orbitly has routed traffic straight to that dedicated pool for low-latency. if we drain we should make sure routing policy moves to their backup pool to avoid 502s. recommend setting temporary route -> orbitly-backup-dedpool.

leah: running drain command:

```
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

leah: cordon done. starting evict. will watch pod evict events.

sanjay: past logs show repeated GPU fan errors. grabbing dmesg and nv logs.

```
# ssh gpu-node-7
$ dmesg | tail -n 40
[12345.678] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:01:00: GPU fan speed unexpectedly dropped to 0
[12345.789] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, GPU hangs
[12346.000] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: fatal exception
```

leah: interestingly this is a preemptible host (spot) but we see clear hardware fan failure prior to preemption. marking root cause candidate: hardware thermal/fan failure -> kernel panic.

dmitri: hw-ops here. i can replace the node but ETA ~45m for swap + reimage (we have spare GPU blades at parity). do you want a full RMA or hot-swap?

sanjay: hot-swap please, aim for minimal pool downtime. leah, can you reroute orbitly traffic now? aj, can you confirm backup pool has capacity for orbitly models without breaking SLOs?

aj: backup pool has 60% headroom. i'll update routing policy for orbitly to prefer orbitly-backup-dedpool and fall back to hosted for low-priority requests. snippet i pushed to routing: 

```
policy:
  - route: orbitly-backup-dedpool
    priority: 1
  - route: hosted-generic
    priority: 2
```

aj: pushing change now. watch for model errors, i will also enable temporary request-throttling for heavy batch jobs.

leah: pods evicted gracefully. 2/3 service pods restarted in backup pool. batch job queued; manual resume later.

ops-bot: notice: orbitly route update applied by aj at 2026-03-15T14:03:10Z :white_check_mark:

tina-cs: tina-cs here. communicating to Orbitly support channel now. Drafting message: 

"Orbitly — we're experiencing a dedicated GPU node hardware failure in your dedicated pool. We've routed production traffic to a backup pool and are replacing the faulty node. We anticipate minimal impact; some batch jobs may be delayed. ETA for full replacement: ~45m. We'll update you with any changes."

sanjay: good. @tina-cs please include that there was no data loss and model state was persisted (KV cache not replicated across nodes by design). mention potential transient latency spike for a few requests.

tina-cs: updated message and sent to Orbitly. customer acknowledged, asking for ETA and whether this will affect SLA credit.

dmitri: starting hot-swap now. powering down blade, swapping fan assembly and nvme. reimage will start automatically. i'll post progress updates.

leah: monitoring routing metrics. 99p latency for orbitly route bumped from 120ms -> 260ms for ~3m during switchover, now down to ~140ms. error rate stayed <0.5%.

sanjay: if hardware repair takes >30m escalate to SRE lead for priority replacement. setting reminder.

dmitri: 30m update: hardware swap complete, reimage started (cloud-init). node shows as Ready -> NotReady -> Ready sequence in k8s.

```
$ kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-node-7
gpu-node-7   Ready   4d\n
```

leah: rejoined pool and kubelet re-registered. rebalancing pods back. i'll cordon drain the backup pool afterwards to shift any remaining load back to primary if you want.

aj: i'm keeping routing policy pinned to backup for another 10m to ensure warm caches. after that we'll route back. will schedule a canary first.

tina-cs: informed Orbitly of repair completion and next steps. they asked for postmortem with timeline and mitigation plan.

sanjay: agree. we'll produce a postmortem covering: root cause (fan failure -> kernel panic), why preemptible status didn't mask failure, mitigation performed (automated drain, routing change, hot-swap), customer-facing comms, and follow-ups (improve cache replication, add health-probe to detect fan drop earlier, consider non-spot hosts for critical low-latency tenants).

leah: closing tasks: uncordon gpu-node-7, remove temporary routing after cache warm, verify no residual evicted pods.

ops-bot: incident 1878001234 transitioned to RESOLVED by sanjay at 2026-03-15T14:18:40Z :white_check_mark:

sanjay: resolved for now. postmortem owner: leah. follow-up ticket in backlog: INFRA-4897 (hardware monitoring + early fan-failure alerts).

dmitri: closing hardware ticket, leaving RMA open for tracking spare parts.

leah: will draft postmortem and ping eng-ops for review. thanks everyone for quick responses. :thumbsup:
